statement0:
The word "for" is mentioned two or more times in 92.2% of psychology papers' Results sections, as of 2020-2024.

Among 2020-2024 papers containing "for" , 26.9% of reported significant p-values (p < .05) are fragile (.01 ≤ p < .05) - i.e., barely fall under the standard significance threshold. This is similar to the typical Psychology paper (median shown for reference); relative to other words, papers with "for" are in the top 58th percentile of fragile p-value percentages (lower = better). Note, strong/weak p-values highly predict replicability(see Supplemental Materials 7.3 of the associated paper).
statement1: As of 2020-2024, papers containing "for" tend to be published in lower impact factor journals (16th percentile among all words) and tend to be cited less (35th percentile word). In general, this word is negatively associated with university ranking, such that higher-ranked institutions are less likely to publish papers containing "for" (29th percentile).
